memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess result reproducibility if the system version used in the field deployment is not disclosed.
Record changes in system configurations, field procedures, and data collection tools during deployment, along with their timestamps and rationales.
The history of deployment versions and configuration changes provides necessary evidence for interpreting results from different field sites.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate ethical and methodological concerns. The reference focuses on participant burden, access, privacy, equipment, prototype expectations, and recruitment authority, while the compared frame focuses on deployment versioning, change records, reproducibility, and cross-site interpretation.

relations.reason: Both reference memories express the same one-sided task-level burden-to-mitigation requirement, respectively as a proposal instruction and an ethics-review criterion.
relations.summary: Expected participant burdens and mitigation strategies should correspond to each user study task and be reviewable on that basis.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers disclosing deployed system versions, recording timestamped deployment changes and rationales, and using version histories to interpret reproducibility and cross-site results.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers task-level burden safeguards, accessibility delivery, data de-identification, equipment loans, prototype disclosure, repeated-study limits, proposal framing, and recruitment power concentration.
